source_title: Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals
quote_or_excerpt:
Of course Comp is not the kind of complete ordinal logic that we should
really wish to use. The use of Comp does not make it any easier to see
that A is dual. In fact, if we really want to use an ordinal logic a proof,
of completeness for that particular ordinal logic will be of little value; the
ordinals given by the completeness proof will not be ones which can easily
be seen intuitively to be ordinals. The only value in a completeness proof
of this kind would be to show that, if any objection is to be raised against
an ordinal logic, it must be on account of something more subtle than
incompleteness.

location.section: Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals

observation: Turing 明确判断，Comp 虽是完备的序数逻辑，但其完备性证明给出的序数难以被直觉识别为序数，因此不是人们真正希望使用的那类逻辑。
